clue.text: Typical bear saw red on a regular basis

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it, put up with it

indicators.note: on a regular basis asks for every other letter of saw red, the even ones

explanation.surface: An everyday bear sees red now and then: a grumpy animal with a recurring temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something typical is the norm, the usual standard of its kind.

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A bad smell coming off a little fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pong is British slang for a bad smell, and a stench is a strong foul odour.

clue.text: PM following nobody except Carrie, ultimately

parts.note: after means following

indicators.note: except says a letter is excluded from the word for nobody

parts.note: nobody is no one

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the last letter of Carrie

explanation.surface: A prime minister succeeding nobody but Carrie, as if Carrie Symonds held office first.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem, the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, labels the hours after midday.

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
to pound something is to ram it

explanation.surface: Paying five hundred pounds for tiny tots of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: '500 pounds' reads as money, but pounds is a verb meaning batters.
explanation.definitionFit: Drams are small measures of spirits, especially whisky.

indicators.note: to cook something is to tamper with it, so the letters of Precise are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: Meticulous cooks rely on written instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'cooks' rearranges PRECISE, and precise cooks do follow these.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipes are written cooking instructions that careful chefs follow exactly.

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter of the verb is dropped, so it has no end

parts.note: to talk about something is to discuss it

explanation.surface: Someone droning on without stopping about a track-and-field competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus is a field event in athletics where a heavy disc is thrown.

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are rubbishy and get rearranged

explanation.surface: Trousers that fit well get no grumbles from the wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a noun for trousers; it is the anagram signal, British slang meaning poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness or ailment, and an infection is one.

indicators.note: under says the last piece comes below the others in this down answer

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
an object is an aim, a goal

explanation.surface: Grip a big item beneath one's cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim is to assert or hold that something is so.

clue.text: Alien starts to slide towards Ripley with fury

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: fury is anger

explanation.surface: In the film Alien, the monster lunges furiously at Ellen Ripley.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a stranger, an outsider from elsewhere.

definitions.meaning: to hold someone spellbound, to grip their attention

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are said differently: EN-trance (a doorway) and en-TRANCE (to enthral).
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway is a way in; to enthral an audience is to grip it.

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
honest dealing is fair dealing

explanation.surface: A fine and honest business sounds like an endorsement of a trustworthy firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or concern, as in 'that is my business'.

definitions.meaning: a jack is a ship's ..., as in the Union Jack
golfer Jack Nicklaus aims at the ... marking the hole

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it looks like golfer Jack Nicklaus; split, Jack is one sense and the golf pin another.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is a naval ensign; a golfer aims for the flagstick on the green.

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: not half says only one half of the word rescue is kept, here its first half

explanation.surface: Someone asked if they fret about being rescued answers emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it literally halves rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cares are troubles or anxieties, the things that weigh on the mind.

clue.text: More than one copper coin pal exchanged with me

indicators.note: exchanged suggests the letters swap places with each other into a new order

explanation.surface: Swapping a copper coin with a friend, as children might trade pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a copper is a policeman, and a policeman is 'more than' one copper coin, so the money surface doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is British slang for a police officer, so a policeman is a copper, worth more than a penny.

clue.text: Cars finally get stuck in boggy areas

indicators.note: stuck in says one piece is lodged inside the other

parts.note: moors are open, often boggy, upland areas

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word get

explanation.surface: Cars eventually get bogged down in marshy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Motors is an informal word for cars, as in 'nice motor'.

clue.text: Making a speech about exercises working

indicators.note: about says the speech word goes around the exercises

parts.note: orating is making a speech
PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: Talking about workouts while doing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Operating means functioning, running, in action.

clue.text: Notice good politicians taken in by cock and bull story

indicators.note: taken in by says the politicians are held inside the story

parts.note: a cock-and-bull story is an unlikely tale, a lie
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Seeing that decent politicians have been fooled by a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: To glimpse is to catch sight of, to notice briefly.

parts.note: a prom is a formal dance, a ball

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the word net has gone wrong, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A shot that hits the net, sadly, in tennis or football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' is the dance, not something struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominent means conspicuous, standing out, which is striking.

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are scattered through the air into a new order

explanation.surface: Father piloting an altered American jet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of dad's stands for 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusted means altered slightly, changed to suit.

indicators.note: protecting means the teachers surround and shelter the other word

parts.note: dons are university teachers, especially at Oxford and Cambridge
key means important, as in a key point

explanation.surface: Academics shielding important animals, perhaps in a conservation project.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkeys are domestic beasts of burden, a kind of animal.

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: gas is informal for idle talk

explanation.surface: An oriental thinker gives an unsettling lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sage is a wise person, a philosopher.

clue.text: Haphazard behaviour, and ominous to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Behaviour described as erratic and somewhat menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means without pattern or plan, done by chance.

parts.note: dress means clothing

explanation.surface: Asking whether European clothing is correct, then confirming it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Right' gives R; the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress is to set right a wrong; as a noun it is reparation.

clue.text: Remained sober by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the answer is heard like a word meaning sober

parts.note: staid means sober, serious

explanation.surface: Stayed sober, apparently, after a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayed is the past tense of stay, to remain.

clue.text: The same United Nations money that might be given back by Germany

parts.words: money that might be given back
parts.note: change is the money a shop hands back after a purchase
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: UN funds that Germany might repay: a story of international finance.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchanged means unaltered, still the same as before.

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: empty means the inside letters of room are removed, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A tea room with no customers still has its charm.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of room's stands for 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is attractiveness, the power to delight and appeal.

definitions.meaning: Jonathan ... was the Irish writer of Gulliver's Travels

explanation.definitionFit: Swift means quick; Jonathan Swift is the satirist behind Gulliver's Travels.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
to till is to dig or cultivate soil

explanation.surface: Using spades to dig the garden regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means nevertheless, which is all the same.

indicators.note: returning says the word for the smoke comes back, read backwards

parts.note: a cigar is a smoke

explanation.surface: An awful period in which smoking came back into fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic means dreadful, calamitous, like a tragedy.

clue.text: Delegate — one with precise manner of speaking

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
very means precise, as in 'the very spot'

explanation.surface: A delegate known for exact, careful speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery is the way a speaker presents a speech: pace, tone and diction.

clue.text: Editor reflected about American magazine's cost

indicators.note: about says the reversed editor goes around the rest
reflected means the editor's letters are mirrored, read backwards

explanation.surface: An editor muses on what an American magazine costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is informal for the price or bill, as in 'what's the damage?'

clue.text: Remote island, possibly oldest around area

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the area
possibly says the letters of oldest may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A far-flung island, perhaps the oldest one in the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges OLDEST to SOLTED, and 'around' puts A inside it: SOLATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means cut off and far from others, which is what remote describes.
